texts: The lanterns of three Cliff Path stations burn extra mire-essence.
What happens to the lanterns of those stations?

fields.sentence: The lanterns of three Cliff Path stations burn extra mire-essence.

q1_issues.issue: The per-member distribution rule reuses the single constant sk_mire_essence_1 as each member's Patient, asserting that every lantern burns that same portion, where the object is an indefinite mass introduced under the distributed plural and so is a dependent existential (a Skolem term of $x per the dependent-existential rule).

q2_gaps: "extra" as an above-normal / additive quantity modifier on a mass noun: the Degree quantity-marker vocabulary is a closed three-symbol set (excessive / insufficient / sufficient) tied to too much / too little / enough, and no other carrier is defined for a comparative-quantity modifier with an elided standard
review.notes: Statement 11 coins a fourth quantity marker, (Degree sk_mire_essence_1 quantity extra), for the gap above. The Northgate-spokesman Possession for "Cliff Path stations", the group+Cardinality+group-event+per-member-rule shape for the counted plural, and the mire_essence genus (noun modifier not exposed) are all correct.

issues.reason: The indefinite mass object under a distributed plural is a dependent existential, which Quantifiers, generics & scope encodes as a Skolem function of the bound variable (a shared constant is reserved for 'the same Y' / 'a certain Y', and the ambiguity default gives the first — universal — quantifier wide scope), so (Patient (sk_burn $x) sk_mire_essence_1) asserts that every lantern burns one and the same portion, which the text does not state.

gaps_confirmed: "extra" as an above-normal / additive quantity modifier on a mass noun: the (Degree <N> quantity <marker>) vocabulary is the closed set excessive / insufficient / sufficient tied to too much / too little / enough, and an elided-standard comparative quantity word has no other carrier — Comparatives & degree only says to drop such a comparative and record the gap
new_gaps: A mass object under a per-member distribution rule has no defined shape: the dependent-existential machinery is written for count witnesses, and nothing relates a member's Skolem portion (sk_mire_essence $x) to the group event's mass witness sk_mire_essence_1 — the Partitives mass apparatus (Member + PartOf + ProportionOf, no GroupOf) is not wired into distribution rules, so the two would sit unconnected

A modified bare mass object in a habitual clause has no settled filler: Existential and Coordination & plurals keep the bare kind symbol for a non-specific / kind-level object ("grows wheat", "pays tax"), but a modifier like "extra" needs an individual bearer and no rule says a modifier promotes the kind filler to a witness
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form makes the burned essence a dependent existential inside the rule — (Implication (PartOf $x sk_lanterns_1) (And (Member (sk_burn $x) burn) (Agent (sk_burn $x) $x) (Patient (sk_burn $x) (sk_mire_essence $x)) (Member (sk_mire_essence $x) mire_essence))) — with the quantity modifier likewise per member, though that modifier's own carrier stays gap-blocked.
adjudication.notes: Everything else checks out: the Northgate-style Possession for "Cliff Path stations", the name-internal kind atom (Member cliff_path path), group + Cardinality + group event + per-member rule for the counted plural, Patient for burn's consumed object, no tense atom on the simple-present habitual, and mire_essence carrying its genus only (a noun modifier is never exposed). I agree with the reviewer that the coined marker in (Degree sk_mire_essence_1 quantity extra) is graceful improvisation in gap territory rather than a defect — it is well-typed and true of the text, and Core patterns bars silently dropping a stated qualifier.

fields.sentence: What happens to the lanterns of those stations?

q2_gaps: An open-verb undergoer question ("what happens to X?"): the Queries section supplies only the agent-side "What does X do?" template, and with the verb left as an unknown the undergoer's role slot is verb-dependent (Patient for a change-of-state verb, Theme for displacement, Experiencer for a state), with no licensed union over role slots — the Dual-storage union pattern lists its instances explicitly and role alternation is not among them.
review.notes: The context-identified referent "the lanterns of those stations" is correctly bound as the constant sk_lanterns_1 directly rather than rebuilt from its GroupOf/Possession atoms, per the Input section. Consequence of the gap: the sole Patient branch matches nothing stored under Theme or Experiencer.
